question: Once a spare index's lease has been closed with reason 'Swap', is it guaranteed that no later action can rewrite that closure reason back to 'None'?
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: A lease closure reason is write-once: once a lease is closed with a reason, that reason is immutable (closure records are append-only, never rewritten).

question: In every reachable state, is a spare index whose lease closed with reason 'Swap' required to have no live intent pod (its funded capacity now carries the swapped-in active work)?
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Funded capacity is conserved: capacity already consumed by a swap cannot simultaneously back a standby spare pod — no slot is spent twice.

question: Is the sum of live spare pods plus swap-consumed spare slots always at most the run's declared spare count (3)?
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: A reconciler never over-provisions beyond the declared desired count; live replicas plus retired-but-charged slots stay within the funded budget.

question: After a TopUp, must every spare index that has not been consumed by a swap have a live intent pod, regardless of which indices went missing and in what order?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => post['reason'+i] === 'Swap' || post['pod'+i] === 'Live')
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Reconciliation converges: one reconcile pass drives observed state to desired state for every slot that is still supposed to exist, independent of the order in which slots were lost.

question: If every non-consumed spare index is already live, is TopUp required to be a no-op (no state change at all)?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || ![0,1,2].every(i => pre['reason'+i] === 'Swap' || pre['pod'+i] === 'Live') || [0,1,2].every(i => post['pod'+i] === pre['pod'+i] && post['reason'+i] === pre['reason'+i])
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Reconcile loops are idempotent: re-running against an already-converged state produces no writes.

question: Is a spare index whose lease closed with reason 'Swap' permanently retired, so that no TopUp may ever bring its pod back to 'Live'?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => pre['reason'+i] !== 'Swap' || post['pod'+i] === 'Gone')
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: A slot retired by promotion is not re-created by the reconciler; desired state shrinks by the promoted slots rather than the controller resurrecting them.

question: Can a spare index's closure reason become 'Swap' only as the direct result of a SwapConsume naming that same index?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => [0,1,2].every(i => pre['reason'+i] === 'Swap' || post['reason'+i] !== 'Swap' || (action === 'SwapConsume' && data && String(data.idx) === String(i)))
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Status attribution is precise: a closure reason is stamped only by the event that actually caused that closure, on exactly the object it happened to.

question: Does an event naming one spare index (LosePod or SwapConsume) leave all other indices' pods and closure reasons completely untouched?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => (action !== 'LosePod' && action !== 'SwapConsume') || !data || [0,1,2].every(i => String(i) === String(data.idx) || (post['pod'+i] === pre['pod'+i] && post['reason'+i] === pre['reason'+i]))
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Replica slots are independent: an event affecting one replica must not mutate a sibling replica's object or status (no wrong-sibling closures).

question: Is SwapConsume(idx) only permitted when index idx currently has a live spare pod for the swap to land on?
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: A node-failure swap lands on real, funded standby capacity, so it can only consume a spare that currently exists.

question: Does SwapConsume(idx) always leave index idx with its pod 'Gone' and its closure reason 'Swap'?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'SwapConsume' || (!!data && post['pod'+data.idx] === 'Gone' && post['reason'+data.idx] === 'Swap')
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Promotion of a spare both removes the standby pod and closes its lease with reason 'Swap' atomically.

question: Does LosePod(idx) leave the closure reason of index idx unchanged (an external eviction or drain must never be recorded as 'Swap')?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'LosePod' || (!!data && post['reason'+data.idx] === pre['reason'+data.idx] && post['pod'+data.idx] === 'Gone')
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Externally caused disappearance of a replica is distinguishable from deliberate promotion; only the latter sets the 'Swap' closure reason, so the former stays re-provisionable.

question: Is TopUp purely additive — never turning a live spare pod 'Gone' and never modifying any closure reason?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => (pre['pod'+i] !== 'Live' || post['pod'+i] === 'Live') && post['reason'+i] === pre['reason'+i])
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: A top-up reconciler only creates missing objects; it never deletes surviving ones nor rewrites lease status.

question: If an index lost its pod without a swap (reason still 'None'), is it guaranteed that the very next TopUp restores it to 'Live', even when a lower- or higher-numbered index was already consumed?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => !(pre['pod'+i] === 'Gone' && pre['reason'+i] === 'None') || post['pod'+i] === 'Live')
domain: Kubernetes-style gang/GPU run controller: spare capacity reconciliation and lease closure
norm: Out-of-order loss of a replica does not strand it: the reconciler fills the genuinely-missing indices rather than a prefix of the index range.
